name: Moonbase
overview: Moonfin server plugin for Jellyfin with web app hosting, settings sync, theming, and Seerr integrations
description: Moonbase is the Moonfin server plugin for Jellyfin, powering settings sync, the Moonfin Web app at /Moonfin/Web/, a built-in theme editor with custom theme APIs, media bar and ratings integrations, and Seerr proxy/SSO with admin defaults and broadcasts across Moonfin clients.

versions.changelog:
Sixth fork release, on upstream commit a365f72 (Moonbase 2.4.0 plus the keyboard style and Peek Home Rows settings).

New from upstream: the Peek Home Rows setting (Moonbase, User defaults, media bar). It shows the top half of the first home row along the bottom of the media bar on TV and desktop, and the Smart TV app can now get a server default for it. The Banner style ignores it.

Nothing else changed. The TMDB routes, the TV app settings editor and the secondary subtitle defaults from 2.4.0.5 are as they were. The web app is still upstream's 2.4.0 build, unchanged. Push notifications through Moonfin's hosted relay are still off in this fork.

Fifth fork release, on upstream commit 1c86196 (Moonbase 2.4.0 plus the keyboard style setting).

Changed: the Moonbase User defaults tab no longer has a separate 'All TV app settings' subtab. Each Moonfin TV app setting now sits in the category of the app's own screen (Subtitles, Subtitle Customization, Audio, Quality & Decoding and so on), next to the settings every Moonfin app shares. The audio codec order is a sortable list like the button layouts.

Added: the second subtitle track of the TV app (preferred language, size, vertical offset, color) can have a default. The Row Image Type and per-row image choices offer Backdrop and Logo as well as Poster, Thumbnail and Banner, in both the Classic and the Modern row style. The detail page and on-screen button lists know the buttons only the TV app has (Add to collection, Playback info, Artwork, Episodes, Sleep timer), so saving the page keeps them in an arrangement.

The web app is still upstream's 2.4.0 build, unchanged. Push notifications through Moonfin's hosted relay are still off in this fork.

Fourth fork release, on the same upstream base as before (Moonbase 2.4.0 up to upstream commit e848699).

Fixed: the Moonfin button in Jellyfin web (the web app served at /Moonfin/Web/) did not work in releases 2.4.0.1 to 2.4.0.3, because their download did not contain the web app and the page answered 404. The download now carries it, so the button works after an install and after every update. The web app is upstream's Moonfin web build from the 2.4.0 release, unchanged; its source is https://github.com/Moonfin-Client/Moonfin-Core. The download is about 66 MB instead of 2 MB.

Nothing else changed. The TMDB routes, the 102 settings and the editor from 2.4.0.3 are as they were. Push notifications through Moonfin's hosted relay are still off in this fork.

Third fork release, on the same upstream base as before (Moonbase 2.4.0 up to upstream commit e848699).

Fixed: in the All TV app settings editor, two settings now offer the values the Moonfin apps actually write. Max Streaming Bitrate offers Mbps as text, with both forms of Auto (0 for the TV app, auto for the Moonfin app). Screensaver Timeout offers the minute codes both apps read, plus the TV app's 30 and 90 seconds. Before, the editor offered plain numbers (120000000 and 30) that the Moonfin app could not read; a value already saved that way shows as (current) until you pick a new one.

Nothing else changed. The TMDB routes, the 102 settings and everything else from 2.4.0.2 are as they were.

Second fork release, on top of upstream Moonbase 2.4.0 (up to upstream commit e848699), the same base as 2.4.0.1.

New: the Moonbase admin defaults can now hold a default for every setting of the Moonfin Smart TV app. The plugin has 102 new settings, named as the app sends them (subtitle styling, audio codec order and passthrough, accent colors, the skip overlay, the playback time display, the screensaver, trick play and more), and they are merged, resolved and applied to users like the existing ones. A new subtab, All TV app settings, under User defaults lets an admin set them. Not set leaves the user's own choice, a number typed outside its range is moved into it, a value you did not touch is saved as it was, and the settings search finds them.

Kept out on purpose: the app's PIN, kids-mode and auto-login state, and the device switches allowInsecureCerts, pinCodeProtection and useMoonfinPlugin.

Changed: Video Start Delay is now a decimal, because the app moves it in half seconds; a whole number is stored as before. maxBitrate and screensaverTimeout are still stored as text.

The three TMDB routes and everything else from 2.4.0.1 are unchanged. Push notifications through Moonfin's hosted relay are still off in this fork, because that relay's key is not in the download; use your own Firebase service account in Moonbase if you need push.

First Moonbase fork release, on top of upstream Moonbase 2.4.0 (up to upstream commit e848699). The version is upstream's number plus a fork digit, so 2.4.0.1 replaces upstream's Moonbase in place with the same id and keeps its settings.

New: three routes that let the Moonfin Smart TV app get its TMDB text without a TMDB key of its own, using the server-wide TMDB key set in Moonbase. /Moonfin/Tmdb/Details gives a title's name, overview, tagline, season names and next episode. /Moonfin/Tmdb/Season gives a season's episodes with names, descriptions, air dates, crew and guest stars. /Moonfin/Tmdb/Recommendations gives TMDB's recommendations for a title. They answer with TMDB's own field names in the viewer's language, remember answers for 24 hours, and never send the key to a client. They replace the app asking TMDB directly. The existing NextEpisode route is unchanged and still gives the air date.

Included from upstream, not the fork's work: LiveTV incomplete-recording handling and record-future-showings, a Moonbase default for hidden libraries, the Enable SyncPlay user default, and the removal of the legacy jellyseerr routes, settings aliases, ping fields and config migration.

Releases of this fork are published at Licaa21/Plugin, and its catalog lists only the fork's own releases.
